name: Commodity carry (roll yield / basis)

origin.source_title: Facts and Fantasies about Commodity Futures (NBER WP 10595, 2004; Financial Analysts Journal 2006)

how_it_works.simple: Some commodity futures get cheaper the further out you go, so holding them earns a small gain each month as they roll up. Buy those, and sell the ones that work the other way.
how_it_works.analogy: Like renting out a flat where the rent already covers the mortgage; you earn even if the flat's price stays put.
how_it_works.precise: Carry (basis) is the annualized slope between near and next futures prices. Backwardated commodities (high carry) tend to have low inventories and earn higher future returns; a long-short portfolio sorted on carry earns a premium. Koijen, Moskowitz, Pedersen and Vrugt show the same carry signal predicts returns across many asset classes.

rule: Each month end, compute basis = (F_near / F_next - 1) annualized for each commodity; go long the half (or top third) with the highest basis and short the lowest, equal-weighted or rank-weighted; roll before delivery; rebalance monthly.
data_needed: Front and second-month futures prices for 20 or more commodities, daily or monthly
economic_rationale: Low inventories raise both backwardation and expected returns, compensating holders for price risk (Gorton and Rouwenhorst 2006; Koijen et al. 2018).
why_it_might_fail: Carry trades crash together in global recessions (Koijen et al. 2018), and AQR's commodity carry series had an 87% peak to trough loss over its history in the catalog's computation.

After the Koijen et al. working paper.

post_publication_evidence: Bhardwaj, Gorton and Rouwenhorst (2015) find the high minus low basis spread held up out of sample (10.41% a year, Sharpe 1.04, 2005 to 2014), while the long-only commodity risk premium fell to 3.67% a year (Sharpe 0.24). In AQR's century dataset, commodity carry earned a Sharpe ratio of about 0.20 from 2013 to early 2026 (catalog computation).

implementations.notes: Futures trading framework by Rob Carver; the provided rules folder includes ewmac.py (trend) and carry.py. Repo moved from robcarver17/pysystemtrade.

relevance.reason: The commodity analogue of FX carry; useful as a building block and because commodity term structures can inform commodity-currency trades.
